A. History and Development of the Company
Our legal and commercial name is Immutep Limited. We were incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Australia on May 21, 1987. Immutep, formerly called Prima BioMed, was originally created as a mining company (Prima Resources) in Australia in 1987 and was first publicly traded in 1988 on the Australian Stock Exchange. The Company was repositioned as a biotechnology company in 2001 following the acquisition of the rights to develop technologies from the Austin Research Institute (now the Burnet Institute).
In December 2014, we completed the acquisition of Immutep S.A., a private French company. In December 2014, Immutep S.A. underwent a change of company organization and become known as Immutep S.A.S. In November 2017, what was then known as Prima BioMed Ltd, changed its name to Immutep Limited to reflect the new strategic direction and management of the business to focus on the development of its portfolio of LAG-3 based immunotherapy assets.
Our registered office is located at Level 32, Australia Square, 264 George Street, Sydney 2000 New South Wales, Australia and our telephone number is +61 2 8315 7003. Our address on the Internet is www.immutep.com. Our agent for service of process in the United States is Immutep U.S., Inc. The information on, or accessible through, our website is not part of this Annual Report on Form 20-F. We have included our website address in this Annual Report on Form 20-F solely as an inactive textual reference. All information we file with the SEC is available through the SEC’s Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis and Retrieval system, which may be accessed through the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov.
B. Business Overview
Background
Immutep is a late-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 related immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. We are pioneers in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3). Our diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s unique ability to modulate the body’s immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximize value for shareholders.
Our lead clinical candidate is eftilagimod alfa (“efti” or “IMP321”) for the treatment of different types of cancers. Efti is a soluble LAG-3Ig fusion protein that is a first-in-class antigen-presenting cell (APC) agonist designed to capitalize on LAG-3’s unique ability to drive the adaptive and innate immune systems against cancer. Efti binds to and activates antigen presenting cells via MHC II molecules which could lead to expansion and proliferation of CD8+ (cytotoxic) T cells, CD4+ (helper) T cells, dendritic cells, NK cells, and monocytes. It could also upregulates the expression of key biological molecules that further boost the immune system’s ability to fight cancer. Efti’s favorable safety profile enables various combinations, including with anti-PD-[L]1 immunotherapy and/or chemotherapy.
In March 2026, following a planned interim futility analysis, Immutep discontinued TACTI-004 (NCT06726265; KEYNOTE-F91), its registrational Phase III trial of efti in combination with an anti-PD-1 therapy and chemotherapy in 1st line non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and commenced an orderly wind-down of the trial together with a comprehensive root cause analysis, which remains ongoing.
The Company has completed the randomized Phase IIb TACTI-003 (NCT04811027) trial of efti in combination with an anti-PD-1 therapy in 1st line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and has received positive and constructive feedback from the FDA supporting further clinical development of the combination in patients with PD-L1 CPS <1 tumors. The Phase II portion of AIPAC-003 (NCT05747794), an integrated Phase II/III trial evaluating efti in combination with standard-of-care paclitaxel for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer (MBC), was completed, and the study was formally closed effective June 30, 2026. Efti has also been evaluated in investigator-initiated trials, including, for example, in a Phase I trial platform in a variety of solid tumors called INSIGHT (NCT03252938) and a Phase II trial evaluating efti in combination with radiotherapy and pembrolizumab in soft tissue sarcoma, called EFTISARC-NEO, which met its primary endpoint.
During fiscal 2026, Immutep also entered into a strategic licensing agreement with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories (Dr. Reddy’s), granting Dr. Reddy’s the exclusive right to develop and commercialize efti in all markets worldwide excluding the Immutep Territory. The Immutep Territory consists of the United States, Canada, Europe (excluding the Russian Federation and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)), Japan and Greater China.
Efti has also been evaluated as part of a combination therapy with an immune checkpoint inhibitor in 1st and 2nd line non-small cell lung carcinoma as well as 2nd line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in a Phase II clinical trial, called TACTI-002 (NCT03625323). Additionally, efti has completed a Phase IIb clinical trial as a chemo-immunotherapy combination for metastatic breast cancer termed AIPAC (NCT02614833), and a Phase I combination therapy trial in metastatic melanoma termed TACTI-mel (NCT02676869).

Operations Summary
Immutep has administrative offices in Sydney, Australia,and Berlin, Germany. We also have a laboratory located close to Paris, France for the conduct of research and development relating to the LAG-3 program, under which we have four clinical-stage product candidates: efti, IMP761, IMP701 and IMP731. Background IP supporting the development of LAG-3 products was licensed from Merck Serono in 2002. Development milestones and royalties are payable on earnings of efti, IMP701 and IMP731. Further details are provided under the intellectual property section. As of June 30, 2026, we employed 46 people. Our internal staff manages the Company’s finances, business development, intellectual property, investor relations, oversight of manufacturing, and clinical development. We make extensive use of outside contractors and consultants to help manage and conduct manufacturing and clinical trials.

The following risks relate specifically to our business and should be considered carefully. Our business, financial condition and results of operations could be harmed by any of the following risks. As a result, the trading price of our ordinary shares and our American Depositary Shares, or ADSs, could decline and the holders could lose part or all of their investment.
Risks Related to Our Business
We have a history of operating losses and may not achieve or maintain profitability in the future.
We have experienced significant recurring operating losses and negative cash flows from operating activities since inception. For example, for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, we had net losses of A$79.3 million and A$61.4 million, respectively.
We are a development stage biotech company developing pharmaceutical product candidates and the success of our product candidates is therefore uncertain. We focus on the development of immunotherapeutic products for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases. We have product candidates: eftilagimod alfa (International Nonproprietary Name (INN): eftilagimod alfa) (also known as “efti” or “IMP321”), IMP701 (also known as “LAG525” or INN: ieramilimab), IMP731 (previously also known as “GSK’781”) and IMP761, all of which are related to lymphocyte activation gene 3, or LAG-3, a gene linked to the regulation of T cells in immune responses. Of these, efti and IMP 761 are the subject of active programs.
We expect to continue to incur losses from operations for the foreseeable future and expect the costs of drug development to increase in the future as more patients are recruited to our clinical trials. In particular, we expect to continue to incur significant losses in carrying out clinical trials of efti and IMP761 as well as from ongoing research and preclinical development in terms of immunotherapy product candidates. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with the development, manufacturing, sales, and marketing of therapeutic products such as efti and IMP761, we may experience larger than expected future losses and may never become profitable.
Moreover, there is a substantial risk that we, or our development or collaboration partners, may not be able to complete the development of our current product candidates or develop other pharmaceutical products. It is possible that none of them will be successfully commercialized, which would prevent us from ever achieving profitability.
We have no medicinal products approved for commercial sale and no source of consistent material revenue.
Currently, we have no products approved for commercial sale and to date have not generated material revenue from product sales. We are largely dependent on the future success of our product candidates.
The LAG-3 related product candidates were acquired by us through the acquisition of the French privately owned and venture capital backed company Immutep S.A., a biopharmaceutical company in the field of Immuno-Oncology in December 2014. This acquisition significantly expanded our clinical development product portfolio to other categories of immunotherapies. It also provided the business with pharmaceutical partnerships.

We have now four LAG-3 product candidates or programs. The most advanced of the four is efti (INN: eftilagimod alfa). Efti is a recombinant protein typically used in conjunction with other therapies (e.g., chemotherapy or other immunotherapy) to amplify a patient’s immune response. We have entered into three clinical trial collaboration and supply agreements with Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway/Kenilworth, NJ, USA (known as MSD outside the United States and Canada), through a subsidiary, to evaluate the combination of our immune activator, efti, with MSD’s anti-PD-1 therapy pembrolizumab in Phase II and Phase III clinical trials. We have also entered into two clinical trial collaboration and supply agreements with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, and Pfizer for Phase I clinical trials to evaluate the clinical benefits of combining our immune activator, efti, with avelumab, a PD-L1 blocking antibody. In China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, the exclusive development and commercialization rights to efti are held by our licensee EOC Pharma.
Our second LAG-3 product candidate is IMP701 (INN: ieramilimab, also known as LAG525), an antagonist antibody that acts to stimulate T cell proliferation in cancer patients. IMP701 was fully licensed to CoStim Pharmaceuticals, which was subsequently acquired by Novartis. In August 2026, the exclusive license and collaboration agreement was terminated on notice from Novartis, and Novartis will assign its ownership interest in the jointly owned LAG-3 patents arising under the collaboration to Immutep S.A.S. Our third LAG-3 product candidate is IMP731, a depleting antibody that could remove T cells involved in autoimmunity. IMP731 was licensed to a major pharmaceutical company and has been transferred back to Immutep. Our fourth LAG-3 product candidate is IMP761, a clinical-stage product candidate which is being developed as our first agonist antibody of LAG-3 for application in autoimmune disease. We have discontinued our early-stage small molecule anti-LAG-3 research program, although our exclusive license agreement with Cardiff University has not been terminated. In addition to these products, Immutep has a dedicated R&D laboratory close to Paris with ongoing research capabilities as well as external research collaborations. Immutep also currently generates modest income from sales of LAG-3 research reagents.
Our ability to generate potential future product revenue depends on a number of factors, including but not limited to our ability to:
•
successfully complete preclinical and clinical development of, and receive regulatory approval for, our product candidates;
•
set an acceptable price for our products, if approved, and obtain adequate coverage and reimbursement from third-party payors;
•
obtain commercial and clinical quantities of our products, if approved, at acceptable cost levels; and
•
successfully market and sell our products, if approved.
There can be no assurance that our or our partners’ ability to develop any product candidate will be successful, or that our ability to obtain the necessary regulatory approvals with respect to any of the foregoing will be successful. As a result, the prolonged inability to generate revenue may adversely impact our business operations.
The increase in expenses may adversely impact our business if our sources of funding and revenue are insufficient.
We anticipate if further development of efti was to continue that the potential costs related to the clinical trials will increase and we will require additional funds to achieve our long-term goals of commercialization and further development of efti and other product candidates.
